questions.question: What format does PhoneFSM accept?
options: Any twelve characters from the alphabet
A phone number with two digits in every group
Three digits, a hyphen, three digits, a hyphen, and four digits
Only a sequence of hyphens with no digits
questions.explanation: The states encode the pattern \\d{3}-\\d{3}-\\d{4}, reaching accept_state 12 after ten digits and two hyphens.

questions.question: What may PhoneFSM.valid_next return at state 3?
options: The ten digits
An empty list because state 3 is accepting
Every character in the alphabet
questions.explanation: After three digits, state 3 requires the first hyphen before more digits can be consumed.

questions.question: What does PhoneFSM.transition(3, "7") return?
options: None, because state 3 allows only a hyphen
4, because every character advances the FSM
3, because digits are ignored
12, because a digit completes the phone number
questions.explanation: transition checks ch against valid_next(state); a digit is invalid at state 3.

questions.question: How does mask_logits represent a character that is invalid in the current FSM state?
options: It doubles the invalid logit so it is sampled first
It replaces that character logit with negative infinity
It deletes the character from the alphabet permanently
It sets all valid logits to zero and keeps invalid ones unchanged
questions.explanation: softmax treats -inf as zero probability while retaining the full alphabet indexing.

questions.question: Why does generate_constrained produce a string matching the phone regex with the supplied alphabet?
options: It retries unconstrained strings until one happens to match
It copies PHONE_REGEX into the generated output
It samples only characters allowed by the FSM at each state until the accept state
It always returns the same hard-coded phone number
questions.explanation: Every transition is validated before the state advances, so the completed string follows the FSM format.

questions.question: What is the main difference between generate_unconstrained and generate_constrained?
options: The unconstrained version uses real model logits and the constrained version uses no randomness
The constrained version can emit any length, while the unconstrained version stops at state 12
They use different phone formats but the same transition checks
The unconstrained version samples the whole alphabet at every step, while the constrained version masks invalid choices
questions.explanation: Both use toy random logits; only constrained generation applies valid_next and mask_logits before sampling.
